pt.do.luu_y: A phone compass reads magnetic north, which in Vietnam is about 1° off true north — negligible for the 8 directions but it matters near a mountain border. Stand at the front door with your back to the house, hold the phone flat, and keep away from cars, steel posts and speakers.
pt.bd.luu_y_1: A direction taken from two points on a map is relative to true north (no magnetic offset), accurate to about 1–2° when the points are more than 10 m apart.
pt.bd.qua_gan: The two points are too close (under 5 m) — pick a point further out in front to be sure.
pt.bd.luu_y_2: It is still worth checking against a compass at the door if you can.

pt.hk.kiem_huong: The sitting is {lech}° off the centre of {son} (a replacement facing, more than 3°) — a REPLACEMENT chart is drawn by the Shen school mnemonic, with the standard chart's formation alongside for comparison.

pt.cung.hd6.hoi: Which Kua suits Kua {q} when living together?
pt.cung.hd6.dap: The same {nhom}: {ds} — like Kua {q}, all four share the same four good directions. When two people are in different groups, the front door usually follows the main earner, and each person's own space follows their own Kua.
pt.cung.hd7.hoi: If the house faces a weaker direction for Kua {q}, do I need to move?
pt.cung.hd7.dap: No. Eight Mansions looks at many spots, not just the front door: a person with Kua {q} can point the head of the bed, the desk and the stove's control side towards {h1} or {h2}; others in the house with a different Kua arrange their own rooms by their Kua. This is a view for reference, not a reason to sell or heavily renovate the house you live in.
pt.cung.hd8.hoi: If I was born in January or early February, how is my Kua worked out?
pt.cung.hd8.dap: Eight Mansions uses Li Chun (around 3–5 February) as the start of the year: if you were born before that date, use the previous year. Some books use the Lunar New Year — the Feng Shui tool lets you choose and enter your exact date of birth.
